validation.unit: record = GSS-nominated employer (work establishment) linked to one GSS respondent or spouse; 39 records are documented duplicate-employer copies (V3 = 0), leaving 688 distinct establishments per documentation
validation.record_id: V1 (SRL case identification number; unique per record); SRLID/NOSID copies; GSS person link V5/GSSID/ID; duplicate grouping variables DUP, NUMOBS
validation.weights: WEIGHT (RAWWGT x 688/83.637; label 'rawwgt adjusted to n=688'), RAWWGT = 1/NEWTOTAL; no weight variable set in .por header; GSS person weights FORMWT/OVERSAMP not applicable to establishments
validation.missing_values: 970 variables carry declared user-missing codes in the .por (one with a range); technical manual states the original SPSS-X file declared none; several declarations are substantive (e.g. 995 'large number of applications') and some non-substantive codes are undeclared (e.g. 997, 'varies/depends' = 4)

loader_missing_value_handling.por_parser.py (this study): Returns all stored values; SPSS system-missing ('*.') -> None/NaN; declared user-missing codes are returned as stored and the declarations are exposed in metadata.
loader_missing_value_handling.pyreadstat.read_por 1.3.3: No user_missing option for .por; declared user-missing codes are returned as NaN and missing-value declarations are not exposed (missing_ranges empty).
loader_missing_value_handling.haven::read_por(user_na=TRUE): Keeps declared user-missing codes as stored values; declarations exposed in na_values / na_range attributes (labelled_spss).
loader_missing_value_handling.haven::read_por(user_na=FALSE): Declared user-missing codes converted to NA.
